name: Proton-K
best_known_for: The Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — launched every Salyut + Mir + ISS Russian-segment module, every Venera + Vega Venus probe, every Luna sample-return, and every Soviet outer-planet attempt
credit: Three-stage hypergolic vehicle (N2O4 / UDMH) with optional Blok-D / D-1 / D-2 upper stages for high-energy escape missions. 311 launches 1967-03-10 (Proton-K with Soyuz 7K-L1 lunar capsule) through 2012-03-30, with a launch cadence that anchored Soviet planetary science (Venera 9-16, Vega 1/2, Mars-2/-3/-5/-7) and the entire Mir + ISS heavy-module deployment (Zarya, Zvezda, Pirs, Poisk, Rassvet). Replaced by Proton-M (still in service through 2025+); the K + M share the first three stages but differ in avionics + payload fairing options. The Blok-D upper stage was originally developed for the cancelled N1-L3 crewed lunar architecture; finding it a use case on Proton-K kept the heavy-energy Soviet planetary line alive into the 1980s.
